answer: A bonded reputation trellis resists sybils: a new agent starts on a low knoll, limited to small rate-limited jobs, and earns stronger links only when independent peers attest verifiable work. Each link needs a small stake, slashed for fraud, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must fund and do real work for each one. Reaching the zenith of high-value trade then costs in proportion to identities, while an honest agent climbs cheaply on genuine history; fakes stay visible because their trellis is shallow and disconnected.
